Weekly Summary We cover: Why the $6.3bn Binance exploit has had a surprisingly limited impact on markets. Crypto sentiment resetting as Bitcoin holds key technical support. Improving cross-asset conditions ahead of the US midterms, potentially setting up renewed risk appetite. The Binance Hack and What Comes Next Binance Hack: Putting the Headlines Into Perspective Last week’s $6.3bn Binance exploit was the largest crypto hack on record, but we think the headline figure materially overstates the damage. Approximately $2.8bn in stolen assets were rapidly frozen by Circle , Tether and other issuers, while Binance has reportedly replenished 95% of affected funds through its own reserves and insurance fund. The speed of the response demonstrates how the industry’s capabilities have matured, with transparent onchain infrastructure enabling stolen assets to be frozen and traced, materially containing the damage. For perspective, the exploit represented just 3.7% of Binance’s $171bn in customer assets, with the ultimate economic loss considerably smaller. More importantly, Sunday’s $3.6bn in net withdrawals represented just 2.1% of customer assets, suggesting that even the largest hack in crypto history has failed to trigger a meaningful run on the exchange. Binance customer assets and net flows following the $6.3bn exploit. Ultimately, the economic and market impact looks far less consequential than the headlines suggest. We also think it is misguided to frame this as evidence of crypto’s inherent insecurity. The attack reportedly originated from a compromised engineer’s laptop, an operational vulnerability that could just as easily affect a bank or major technology company. Google suffered a corporate database breach in 2025, seven South Korean financial institutions were reportedly compromised in October, and Chinese hackers targeted US government-affiliated firewalls just last week . Cyberattacks are a reality across every major industry, and there is little reason to hold crypto to a different standard. The Impact on Markets Since the exploit, crypto beta (white) and alts (pink) have underperformed, as expected. However, despite a broader risk-off move, crypto beta underperformed US tech by less than 2%, while alts underperformed crypto beta by a further 2%. Given the scale of the largest exploit in crypto history, a ~6% decline in alts is relatively moderate, particularly against an already weak backdrop for sentiment. Cross-asset performance since the Binance exploit (%). Since Friday’s bottom, the reverse dynamic can be seen with crypto leading the recovery, albeit in a measured way. Cross-asset performance since Friday’s bottom. The recovery has been so strong that even some of the hardest-hit assets, such as ETH, have rallied back into their normal trading pattern which is a rare outcome following a shock. Bitcoin touched the 50W MA briefly where it saw strong bids after the market realised the event was relatively contained. The $80k level (Sep resistance/Oct support) will likely act as key resistance, likely leaving BTC to trade between these two levels until a resolution emerges. We can see this in the order book profile where equal bid/ask stacks are placed around these levels… The backing and filling dynamic also makes sense given the US midterms tomorrow, 3 November 2026. The market is unlikely to move with high conviction in the short-term. Crypto Fear & Greed sentiment has fully reset, mirroring the previous cycle when sentiment fell back towards neutral following the first break above the 50-week MA. This is consistent with historical market dynamics, with the surprise increasingly appearing to be to the upside rather than the downside. Yet, alts vs. BTC looks business as usual when you zoom out. Meanwhile, TradFi’s embrace of blockchain infrastructure continues, underscored by Druckenmiller’s latest bet on Hyperliquid’s ecosystem. Risk-On Positioning Over Mid-Terms? At the same time, we see little reason to conclude that the US AI trade, a key driver of broader risk appetite that can funnel into crypto markets, has run its course. Until the underlying technicals suggest otherwise, we remain constructive on the broader market outlook. Hedge funds have undergone their largest de-risking in a decade. Weekly Summary We cover: Accelerating adoption across three emerging on-chain markets. Bearish sentiment diverging from stabilising market technicals. A pivotal week for macro data, central banks and Big Tech earnings. Three Areas of Growth in On-Chain Markets Beyond traditional crypto markets, three emerging areas are seeing accelerating adoption: AI inference, tokenised collectibles and pre-IPO trading. Each demonstrates how blockchain infrastructure is expanding access to new and existing markets. 1. AI Inference: Demand for Cheaper Compute AI token consumption continues to accelerate, creating demand for infrastructure that connects users with cheaper inference capacity. For example, Dolphin.ai operates a marketplace where users can access AI models from competing providers. Inference exchanges such as Surplus take this further, allowing suppliers to compete to fulfil inference requests, routing demand towards lower-cost capacity while improving supplier utilisation. As AI adoption scales, these marketplaces and exchanges are making inference cheaper and more accessible, creating a growing market for the infrastructure connecting supply and demand. 2. Tokenised Collectibles: Trading Card Volumes Accelerate On-chain trading card spending has accelerated, with weekly volumes approaching $100 million , compared with less than $20 million at the start of the year. Pokémon’s 30th anniversary has supported renewed interest, while integrations across Pump.fun, Jupiter and other Solana applications have expanded distribution. These platforms combine familiar collectibles with crypto-native mechanics: instant pack openings, verifiable ownership and immediate liquidity through stablecoin buybacks. Low transaction costs are helping transform a fragmented market into a more liquid and accessible one. 3. Pre-IPO Markets: Bringing Private Companies On-Chain Pre-IPO perpetual futures volumes have surged to approximately $650 million weekly , reflecting demand for exposure to private companies traditionally inaccessible to retail investors. These products allow investors to speculate on private company valuations without owning the underlying shares. Blockchain infrastructure enables global access, continuous trading and price discovery in historically illiquid markets. Demand for exposure to high-profile private companies, particularly in AI, is creating new opportunities for exchanges to monetise these markets through trading fees. Market Is This The Bottom? With the midterms fast approaching, crypto has edged lower following Saturday’s $600m in long liquidations, although Bitcoin has so far held the $80k level. Weekly Summary We cover: Why Bitcoin is absorbing negative macro headlines The growing disconnect between sentiment and price What could drive the next leg higher into year-end Markets Are Refusing to Break Crypto markets are refusing to break, finding clear support above $80k, around early September highs. Global crypto market capitalisation index ($; daily). Markets have had plenty of reasons to sell over the past two weeks. Brent crude surged towards $105, US CPI and PPI surprised to the upside, and concerns over AI financing intensified following CoreWeave’s sell-off. Each would ordinarily weigh on risk assets through higher inflation, tighter monetary policy or weaker growth expectations. Yet Bitcoin has repeatedly found buyers around $80,000, with little sustained downside despite these headwinds. BTC/USD. Bitcoin holds firm despite negative macro headlines. This is particularly constructive following Bitcoin’s breaks below its 200-day and 50-week moving averages, both traditionally bearish momentum signals. When negative news and bearish technicals fail to push prices materially lower, it suggests sellers are becoming exhausted. This is characteristic of bull market behaviour. Nasdaq futures are also up >1% this morning, with AI stocks rebounding strongly and further evidence that sellers are struggling to sustain downside momentum. Sentiment Is Pricing In a Correction That Hasn’t Happened The disconnect between sentiment and price is becoming increasingly pronounced. Since sentiment peaked on 21 September, total crypto market capitalisation has declined just 7%, while Fear & Greed has fallen 38% on an indexed basis. On 4 October, market capitalisation had returned to its September peak, yet sentiment was already 11% lower. The latest Fear & Greed reading of 20 signals Extreme Fear, despite prices holding relatively firm. A similar divergence is visible in equities, with the S&P 500 just 2% below its record closing high despite sentiment reaching Extreme Fear. CNN S&P Fear & Greed Index. Investors are pricing in a much larger correction than markets have delivered. With positioning already cautious, there is less complacency to unwind and greater scope for an upside surprise as confidence returns. Crypto is also showing relative strength, outperforming the Nasdaq 100 by more than 2% last week. This is not simply a market holding its ground in nominal terms, but one beginning to outperform other risk assets. The crypto/NASDAQ ratio over the past week. Looking Ahead China’s Q3 GDP growth of 4.5% beat expectations , providing some support for risk assets. This follows efforts by Chinese authorities to stabilise domestic equities through selling restrictions and state-backed purchases. Nevertheless, markets may remain nervous ahead of the US midterms on 3 November, with hyperscaler earnings over the next two weeks likely to be an important catalyst. Earnings are likely to remain strong, reassuring investors that growth is holding up and AI investment continues to be supported by underlying demand. This could mark a turning point in market momentum , particularly as the midterms approach and another source of uncertainty is removed. The midterms should then remove another source of uncertainty , allowing investors to focus more clearly on year-end positioning. Nate Silver’s latest midterm election forecast. For now, the combination of resilient prices, extreme pessimism and improving relative strength is constructive. Markets are being given reasons to fall, but increasingly refusing to do so. From Record September to Midterm Uncertainty The Look Back Best September on Record Crypto gained 8.3% in September, its strongest September on record. Historically one of the weakest months for digital assets, September has now delivered four consecutive positive returns, challenging its reputation for seasonal weakness. Q3: The Strongest Quarter Since Q4 2024 Total crypto market capitalisation rose 41% in Q3, ending three consecutive quarters of losses. The strongest quarterly performance since Q4 2024 marks a meaningful shift in momentum, suggesting the market recovery is broadening beyond a short-lived rebound. SOL Outperforms BTC for Two Consecutive Quarters SOL outperformed BTC by 12% in Q3, following a 3% gain in Q2. This marks the first consecutive quarters of relative outperformance since early 2024, suggesting investors are moving further out along the risk curve and sustaining allocations beyond Bitcoin. The Now Bitcoin Approaches a Historically Bullish Signal Bitcoin has recovered from a 54% drawdown in July and now trades 33.8% below its all-time high. Historically, after drawdowns exceeding 50%, a recovery above the 30% drawdown threshold has preceded a new all-time high in all seven qualifying instances, with a median wait of just 23 days. Bitcoin’s historical drawdown-to-ATH recovery pattern, with green markers identifying previous bullish signals and arrows showing the subsequent return to all-time highs. A daily close above $88,390, just 5.7% above current levels, would trigger a historically reliable signal that Bitcoin is imminently heading towards new all-time highs. Price Up, Sentiment Down Bitcoin is 3% higher than at its 21 September sentiment peak, yet Fear & Greed has fallen from 59 to 39. Monetary policy uncertainty, inflation concerns, geopolitical risks and the approaching US midterms are weighing on confidence despite improving prices. Such a disconnect suggests investors remain sceptical of the recovery, leaving scope for upside surprises. The approaching US midterms could provide a catalyst as political uncertainty begins to fade… The Look Ahead US Midterms: A Historically Bullish Turning Point US equities have historically performed strongly following midterm elections, with the S&P 500 averaging 13% over the subsequent six months and 14% over twelve months. The latter period has delivered positive returns after every midterm since WWII. With elections approaching in November, the historical pattern suggests political uncertainty could give way to a more supportive backdrop for risk assets, including crypto. Weekly Summary We cover: Why the US wants to promote dollar stablecoins abroad How regulators are building crypto into existing financial frameworks Why banks integrating stablecoin rails marks a shift in adoption From Permission to Integration Over the past two weeks, a series of headlines have pointed to the same shift. Governments, regulators and financial institutions are moving beyond deciding whether crypto belongs within the financial system and towards how to use it. Individually, none of these developments changes the market overnight. Together, they show crypto increasingly being built into the financial system rather than accommodated at its edges. The US Wants to Export Stablecoins — Not Contain Them The Trump administration is considering supporting dollar stablecoin projects overseas, potentially through public-private partnerships involving Treasury, State and the DFC. The stated objectives include reinforcing dollar dominance and increasing demand for US Treasuries. Re7 Take: This reframes stablecoins from a crypto product into an instrument of US monetary power. The US has effectively recognised that dollarisation in the digital economy does not require foreign users to access US banks — blockchains can distribute dollars globally. The second-order implication is particularly interesting: stablecoin growth becomes structurally aligned with US interests. More USD stablecoins → more offshore dollar usage → potentially more demand for the Treasury assets backing them. Banks Are Starting to Use the Rails Citi partnered with Coinbase to enable stablecoin payments for institutional clients, with Coinbase providing crypto infrastructure and Citi handling the banking/settlement side. Re7 Take: The important development isn’t Citi “getting into crypto.” It is the emerging division of labour: banks retain the regulated customer and fiat relationship while crypto-native infrastructure provides the settlement rail. That is a much more credible path to adoption than crypto replacing banks outright. The same convergence is happening in market infrastructure. Hyperliquid perpetual futures data is now live on the Bloomberg Terminal, giving institutional users access to 24/7 pricing across markets including oil, gold and US equities directly within their existing workflow. Crypto Is Being Fitted Into Institutional Portfolio Infrastructure The SEC has proposed a dedicated custody framework for advisers and regulated funds holding crypto, including permitting self-custody in certain circumstances and state trust companies as custodians. The SEC explicitly describes the objective as giving advisers and funds a compliant pathway to crypto exposure. Re7 Take: Institutional adoption ultimately depends less on whether an investment committee likes Bitcoin and more on whether custody, compliance and fiduciary processes permit ownership. Removing those operational constraints expands the addressable pool of capital. The same shift is taking place in the UK, where the focus is increasingly on how tokenisation fits within existing financial markets. The team at Re7 recently discussed the UK’s tokenisation roadmap at the Cross-Border Fund Distribution Conference in London, contributing to the discussion alongside regulators, lawyers and asset managers on where tokenisation is creating value today and what still needs to change for broader institutional adoption. Re7 discussing the UK’s tokenisation roadmap at the Cross-Border Fund Distribution Conference in London. Final Remarks The adoption story is moving from permission to integration. Governments, regulators and financial institutions are starting to use crypto infrastructure rather than simply make room for it. Stablecoins are becoming part of US dollar policy, banks are integrating the rails and regulators are building frameworks around ownership and custody. Crypto is becoming harder to separate from the financial system it was once positioned outside of. Markets remained buoyed by improving macro conditions, with global curves bull steepening and October hike odds falling sharply, alongside improving sentiment as the SEC proposed broader custody options for crypto funds.
